text.p: The transport ministry said on Monday that it has decided to merge the two national airlines, international carrier Lithuanian Airlines and the smaller Lietuva airline, to ease the privatisation of the companies.
"The transport ministry decided today to merge Lithuanian Airlines (LAL) and Aviation Company Lietuva into one," Transport Minister Algis Zhvaliauskas told Reuters.
"We have also asked the civil aviation department of the ministry to draw up the necessary documents for the merger in the next 10 days," Zhvaliauskas added.
Zhvaliauskas also said that the Aviation Company Lietuva will operate as a daughter company of LAL after the merger.
The minister said the move was necessary to speed up the privatisation process of the two companies.
"During the privatisation, both companies will be sold as one," Zhvaliauskas said.
The government earlier this year slated the 100 percent state-run companies for privatisation.
"After the merger of the two companies, we intend to anounce an international tender to draw up a privatisation program," Zhvaliauskas said.
"It could happen at the beginning of June," he added.
